how: Wear the sleep tracker through the main sleep period.
Check last night's time asleep each morning.

why.text: Crews face chronic sleep loss and irregularities in their internal biological clocks.
why.hrp_risk: Risk of Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules

if_abnormal.now: Compare with the crewmember's own normal, not with one night.
if_abnormal.remeasure: Look at the next nights; one short night is common in flight.
if_abnormal.tell_ground: Add the sleep trend to the next ground report.

space_note: NASA schedules an 8.5 hour sleep period (NASA-STD-3001 [V1 6001]). ISS crews actually slept about 6.1 hours a night in flight (Barger 2014). On Earth, adults need 7 or more hours (AASM). No Safety bound: judged against the personal baseline only.
labels: Earth reference, no space data (AASM 7 hours)
